jsonld.description: Free LTV:CAC calculator for D2C brands. Model repeat purchase as a decaying cohort to get lifetime contribution, your LTV:CAC ratio against the 3:1 benchmark, and the month your customer acquisition cost is paid back.

mainEntity.name: What is a good LTV:CAC ratio?

acceptedAnswer.text: 3:1 is the widely used benchmark, three rupees of lifetime contribution for every rupee of acquisition cost. Below 2:1 growth generally burns cash. Far above 4:1 often means you are underspending and leaving growth on the table.

mainEntity.name: Should LTV use revenue or contribution?

acceptedAnswer.text: Contribution. Lifetime revenue flatters the number badly because it ignores COGS, shipping and fees. LTV built on contribution tells you what is actually available to pay for acquisition and overhead.

mainEntity.name: What is CAC payback and why does it matter?

acceptedAnswer.text: CAC payback is the month cumulative contribution from a customer finally equals what you paid to acquire them. It governs how fast you can grow without external funding: a brand with three-month payback can recycle cash four times a year, while a twelve-month payback can only do it once.
